summary: Codenames is a light social word-association party game where two spymasters give one-word clues to help their teammates identify their team's agents on a shared grid of words, while avoiding the opposing team's agents and the deadly assassin. It plays fast, scales to large groups, and lives or dies on the cleverness and wit of the clue-givers.
praised: extremely easy to teach and universally accessible
endlessly replayable with the same components
criticised: heavily dependent on having witty players; weaker with mismatched groups
the assassin can end a game abruptly and feel anticlimactic
language/culture-dependent clues can confuse some players
less fun with only 2-3 people who overlap awkwardly

interaction.kind: team communication and clue-guessing under uncertainty

scoring.why: the team that contacts all of its own agents first wins, with no accumulating point total
